jobs.name: b2b-reply-scanner-hourly
jobs.description: Scan Gmail (a@/f@/ak@) for B2B Ads outreach replies every hour

payload.message:
Run the B2B Ads reply scanner.

Scan Gmail for new Muso Ads outreach replies across these accounts: a@muso.ai, f@muso.ai, ak@muso.ai, aaron.k@muso.ai.

For EACH account, run EXACTLY this command (substitute <ACCT>) and do not add or change flags. The flag that includes message bodies in search results is --include-body; do NOT use --body (that is a gmail send flag and will fail with 'unknown flag --body'):

gog gmail messages search 'in:inbox newer_than:1d ("Muso Ads" OR "Muso.AI" OR "calendar.muso.ai" OR "Private invite" OR "820K" OR "ads to 820K" OR "Reaching 820K" OR "Muso.AI x")' --account <ACCT> --max 50 --include-body --json

Read the JSON straight from stdout. Do not write results to temp files and do not pipe through jq. The Gmail search is bounded to the last day (newer_than:1d, the only valid Gmail unit near this window); from the results keep only messages received in roughly the last 70 minutes (the run cadence) by reading each message's date. Do not rely only on label:"B2B - Ads" because inbound replies may not carry the label.

Filter out internal muso.ai mail, SaaS notifications, DMARC reports, newsletters, spam, unrelated customer support, and unrelated inbox noise. Keep true prospect replies, meeting-booking language, referrals/new points of contact, questions, pricing asks, explicit pass/unsubscribe replies, OOO with useful referral info, and B2B delivery failures/bounces. Deduplicate by Gmail threadId and account.

Current B2B outreach rules:
- Gmail owns send/reply detection.
- NocoDB is read-only and is the source of contact/company context. Look up contact/company when possible.
- Do not write to NocoDB.
- Do not use GHL.
- Do not use Google Sheets.
- Do not move stages.
- Do not auto-reply.
- Do not create Gmail drafts.
- Do not mark messages read.

For every true item, classify it as Replied, Meeting Booked, Referral, Pricing, Question, Interested/send-info, Soft-no/later, Pass, Bounce, OOO, or Other.

Then apply the muso-outreach-reply-responder logic:
- Decide answer vs skip.
- Match sender voice to the receiving account: a@/ak@/aaron.k@ = Aaron, f@ = Fede.
- Pull thread history before drafting if available.
- If answering, provide ONE exact suggested reply whose only goal is a 15-20 minute call.
- Keep warm-thread replies short and playbook-native.
- No em dashes or en dashes.
- Do not create the Gmail draft until Nick or Aaron approves in Slack.

If no actual new B2B prospect replies or B2B bounces are found, final visible message must be exactly: NO_REPLY

If one or more are found, final visible message must be concise Slack mrkdwn for #sales-alerts. For each item:
*New B2B Reply*
From: *<name>* (<company>, <title if known>)
Received on: <account>
Type: *<classification>*
Preview: _<short preview>_
Verdict: answer / skip

*Suggested reply:*
> <exact draft body, as Aaron or Fede would send>

Manual next step: Nick/Aaron approve before any Gmail draft is created. Nick/team updates NocoDB Status manually if needed.

Always emit a visible final assistant message. Never end with thinking-only output.

jobs.name: company-finder-daily
jobs.description: Daily parent company discovery for B2B outreach - finds 5 new companies (matches the skill's per-day design), dedupes, posts to #company-finder for approval

payload.message: Run the muso-outreach-discovery skill. Find 5 new companies matching Muso Ads target verticals (the skill is designed for ~5/day; a 50-company batch posted 8 fake domains + non-music companies on 2026-04-11, see hard-lessons). Dedupe against the NocoDB B2B-Ads Intelligence base — Company Intelligence (mvr6nmzcv7albxt), Contacts Intelligence (m9vsbijhrr9ddeu) AND the Company Seen Ledger (every company ever suggested, including rejected ones) — by piping the UNION of ALL candidates as ONE JSON array into the deterministic dedup script (see below); then additionally drop matches in the GHL B2B-Ads-Clio pipeline and parent-companies.md (subsidiaries of known parents). NocoDB is the canonical store now (it supersedes the old contacts_intelligence/company_intelligence Google Sheet); do NOT dedupe against the Sheet. Score and select top 5. Return the batch as your final output — do NOT post to Slack directly; the cron runner will deliver it to #company-finder for Nick's review. Follow the SKILL.md workflow exactly. If no new companies match, your final assistant reply must be exactly the single token NO_REPLY and nothing else — no preamble, no explanation, no markdown, no punctuation. OpenClaw recognises this token and will silently complete the run without posting to Slack. Reference files are the shared canonical set in /opt/hydra/workspaces/cmo/skills/muso-outreach-engine/references/ (target-verticals.md, parent-companies.md, config.md) — read and write them THERE, never a local copy, and NEVER create files at workspace root. For NocoDB dedup do NOT loop per-candidate or hand-roll jq/while pipelines (they have failed this cron before, and exact (Domain,eq,...) matching leaks duplicates on domain-format variance). Instead run ONE sanctioned call: echo your candidate JSON array and pipe it into `bash /opt/hydra/scripts/company-finder/dedupe-candidates.sh`. It snapshots all three NocoDB tables once, normalizes both sides, self-dedupes the batch (reason "batch"), and returns {new,duplicates,name_flags,stats}; keep ONLY the companies in .new[], drop everything in .duplicates[], and carry any .name_flags[] possible_match notes into the batch for Nick. THEN pipe the .new ARRAY (e.g. `jq '.new'` of the dedup output — NOT `.new[]`, the script requires one JSON array on stdin) through `bash /opt/hydra/scripts/company-finder/verify-candidates.sh`: drop .dead[] (list them as rejects with reason DEAD), keep .blocked[] flagged '⚠ site bot-walled'; its exit 2 / VERIFY_NETWORK_SUSPECT means our egress is suspect — PARTIAL/UNSAFE, not an all-dead batch. web_fetch each survivor's LinkedIn company page for a dated evidence line (no fetchable page = reject NO_LINKEDIN; recalled URLs are not evidence). Read parent-companies.md directly for the SUBSIDIARY filter. The GHL B2B-Ads-Clio pipeline check (IN_GHL) is BEST-EFFORT, not a required gate: attempt it, but if the GHL read fails (e.g. 403 — $GHL_API_KEY is a CMO credential Scout may lack), SKIP IN_GHL, still ship the batch, and flag it '⚠ GHL pipeline filter unavailable' — never fail the batch on GHL. BEFORE returning the batch, record BOTH halves: (a) echo the TERMINAL mechanical rejects (reason DEAD / NO_LINKEDIN / IN_GHL / SUBSIDIARY — NEVER score-cuts, those must stay re-surfaceable) as a JSON array with a reason field per company into `BATCH_SOURCE=cron:company-finder-daily bash /opt/hydra/scripts/company-finder/ledger.sh record-rejects` (idempotent — already-known domains are skipped, not errors), then (b) echo the final batch JSON array into `BATCH_SOURCE=cron:company-finder-daily bash /opt/hydra/scripts/company-finder/ledger.sh suggest` — non-zero exit from suggest means do NOT ship a normal batch (LEDGER_COLLISION = dedupe was skipped/raced, re-run from the dedupe step; other LEDGER_* markers = PARTIAL/UNSAFE naming the marker). Never write to NocoDB any other way — review-time approve/reject flips happen later in the review thread via ledger.sh per SKILL.md Step 8. Avoid mktemp/$TMP scratch dirs and other improvised multi-step shell pipelines. CRITICAL — distinguish a RECOVERED transient error from a genuinely-missing dedupe source. Wrap external API calls (NocoDB, GHL) in try/except and retry once. If the retry SUCCEEDS, print a marker and let that shell/python step exit 0 — never let a recovered hiccup raise or exit non-zero, because a single non-zero exit (even one you recovered from) marks the whole run failed and blocks delivery of your completed batch. BUT the REQUIRED dedupe sources are NocoDB Company Intelligence + Contacts Intelligence + Company Seen Ledger + parent-companies.md (the GHL pipeline is NOT a required source — see the best-effort note above): if any one is STILL unavailable after the retry, do NOT ship a normal batch with incomplete dedupe — your final reply must explicitly name the failed source and either be exactly NO_REPLY or clearly mark the batch as PARTIAL/UNSAFE so Nick knows the dedupe was incomplete. The dedup script already retries NocoDB once internally and, if NocoDB is still unreachable, exits non-zero printing `DEDUP_SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE: <table>` — treat that exit as exactly this required-source-unavailable signal (NO_REPLY or PARTIAL/UNSAFE), not as a crash to ignore.

jobs.name: b2b-meeting-scanner-hourly
jobs.description: Scan a@ Google Calendar for new B2B Ads meeting bookings every hour

payload.message:
Run the B2B Ads meeting scanner.

Detect NEW B2B meeting bookings on the a@muso.ai calendar (meetings CREATED in roughly the last 70 minutes). Run EXACTLY this command and do not add other flags (especially not --fields):

gog -a a@muso.ai calendar events --from=today --days=90 --max=250 --all-pages --json

From the returned events, keep only events that BOTH:
  1) have a "created" timestamp within the last 70 minutes (compare created vs now in UTC), AND
  2) have at least one attendee whose email domain is NOT muso.ai (an external prospect).
Ignore internal-only events, personal events, all-hands, standups, OOO and recurring internal meetings. Deduplicate by event id.

NocoDB is read-only for company/contact context (look up the external attendee's company when possible). Do not write to NocoDB. Do not use GHL. Do not use Google Sheets. Do not move pipeline stages. Do not create, modify, or delete calendar events.

If no qualifying new meetings are found, your final visible message must be exactly: NO_REPLY (uppercase, nothing else). OpenClaw recognises this token and will silently complete the run without posting to Slack.

If one or more qualify, your final visible message must be concise Slack mrkdwn for #sales-alerts, one block per meeting:
*New B2B Meeting Booked*
With: *<name>* (<company>, <title if known>)
When: <event start, with timezone>
Account: a@muso.ai
Attendees: <external attendees>

Manual next step: Nick/Aaron set the prospect's NocoDB Status to Meeting Booked.

Always emit a visible final assistant message. Never end with thinking-only output.
